channel.title: Wire — Engineering
channel.description: Engineering from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Introducing Search for Agents
item.description: Flip one toggle to make your site searchable by AI agents — complete with automatic content indexing, a discoverable search API, and native HTTP QUERY support. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Art of play in the age of AI
item.description: Now that code ships faster than ever, you have more time to spend on projects just for the fun of it. Here's what we can learn through that process as developers. The post Art of play in the age of AI appeared first on The GitHub Blog . (1 source: githubblog)

item.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
item.description: Learn how to assess a legacy application, choose a bounded modernization step, and reuse the method with a GitHub Copilot agent skill. (1 source: githubblog)

item.title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
item.description: GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
item.description: DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Part 2: Generative bidders for ads at Grab
item.description: Introduction Grab runs marketplaces where many important decisions unfold over time, rather than as one-step predictions. Mobility systems need to anticipate how taxi demand and driver supply may evolve across locations and time windows. (1 source: grab)

item.title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
item.description: Frostbite is a general-purpose CPU built around interaction nets, discovered, designed, and verified end-to-end by our AI systems, reaching 4.59x the performance-per-watt of a modern superscalar (dual-issue, in-order) CPU core. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
item.description: ruby2shell lets attackers corrupt memory in default Rails and Sinatra apps without logging in. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for every customer, including Free plans. Upgrade Ruby now, and use the WAF to cover the gap. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
item.description: phpAfterShell is a critical flaw in PHP's default session handler that can lead to code execution. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for all customers, including Free plans, and adds new rules for other PHP flaws fixed in the same release. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
item.description: Five memory corruption bugs in nginx, called nginx2root, can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a server. Here’s how they work, and why origins behind Cloudflare's proxy are shielded from the most serious of these bugs. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
item.description: On November 3, 2026 U.S. voters headed to the polls. Here’s what Cloudflare data across more than 1,400 protected sites tells us about Election Day Internet traffic and cyberattacks. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: The best things in open source are built together
item.description: Introducing Replica and the Open Source Accessibility Framework, new open source projects for collaboration and inclusion. The post The best things in open source are built together appeared first on The GitHub Blog . (1 source: githubblog)
